Complete the following parametric equations generating the hyperbola above in terms of the parameter $t,$ defined for $t\in [-\pi ,\pi ]$ where $t\ne \pm \frac{\pi }{2},$ given that its asymptotes are $y=\pm \frac{4}{\sqrt{5}}x.$

$x=$
{{field-1}}$,\,y=$
{{field-2}}
$\operatorname{tan}⁡t$
worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin with Cartesian equation

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by

$$
x=a\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=b\operatorname{tan}⁡t,
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are positive constants.

The vertices of the hyperbola occur at $(\pm a,0).$ From the graph, we have that $(\sqrt{5},0)$ is a vertex of the hyperbola, so $a=\sqrt{5}.$

The asymptotes of a horizontal hyperbola are $y=\pm \frac{b}{a}x.$ In our case, the asymptotes are $y=\pm \frac{4}{\sqrt{5}}x,$ and so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{b}{a} & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{b}{\sqrt{5}} & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}} \\ b & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the hyperbola are

$$
x=\sqrt{5}\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=4\operatorname{tan}⁡t.
$$
